To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The coronavirus PLpros are a promising target for antiviral drugs, but they are difficult to inhibit because of the lack of a defined binding site.
the interaction of PLpros from different coronaviruses with the human ISG15 and the ISG15 homologues from the mouse and hamster is highly specific, with only a few exceptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms of the coronavirus papain-like proteases (PLpros) that are responsible for the processing of viral proteins and for the antagonization of interferon (IFN) stimulated genes (ISG) 15.
the structural biology of the coronavirus papain-like proteases and their interaction with the host antiviral protein IFIT5.
the development of a novel, noninvasive, and cost-efficient method to assess the effects of the environment on the human microbiome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLpro from the SARS-CoV-2 is the best inhibitor of the tested species.
the interaction of PLpros and ISG15 from different species is not only species-dependent, but also dependent on the individual PLpro.
the PLpros from different species of coronavirus are structurally and functionally conserved and that they are able to interact with IFIT5 from the same or different host species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a common structural feature of PLpro from different coronavirus species and that we have identified the molecular basis for the inhibition of PLpro by IFITM3.

we have shown that the PLpro of SARS-CoV-2 can bind to ISG15, and that the binding affinity of ISG15 is higher than the binding affinity of the ISG15 homologue, ISG12, for SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV PLpros.
we have determined the structure and function of the SARS-CoV PLpro, and that we have determined a structure of the SARS-Cov-2 PLpro that has a similar structure and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro is more similar to the MERS-CoV 3CLpro than to the SARS-CoVS-CoV 3Clpro, in terms of its ability to interact with IFIT5.
the coronavirus PLpro is a promising drug target for COVID-19 and other coronaviruses.
the PLpros from different species are not interchangeable.
